QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_25

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (open-ended, monthly dealing, equalisation accounting) had HWM NAV/unit of INR 1,200. Current NAV/unit is INR 1,260 (above HWM). A new investor subscribes at INR 1,260. To ensure fairness across unit-holders, what must the fund do?

answer.text: Charge the new investor an equalisation CREDIT on the INR 60 gain above HWM
Charge the new investor an equalisation DEBIT because they enter above HWM
Refund the incentive-fee accrual to the new investor
Reset the HWM to INR 1,260 for the entire unit class

explanation.text: The Logic: When new investors enter above HWM, they would otherwise pay incentive fees on gains THEY didn't participate in. An equalisation CREDIT (paid by the fund via extra units / deposit) compensates them; a DEBIT (extra amount paid by the investor) accrues when they enter BELOW HWM. Resetting HWM disadvantages legacy LPs. The Trap: B swaps credit/debit. C mis-describes the mechanism. D resets HWM which would leak carry to manager at existing LPs' expense. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B Cat III Distributor tests equalisation conceptually; XIX-E tests the accounting treatment. Manager's Pro-Tip: Most Indian Cat III AIFs avoid equalisation by issuing SERIES-OF-UNITS (each monthly subscription = new series with its own HWM). Series-of-units is operationally cleaner but bloats the unit register; pick based on fund-admin capability.
